construction: 136 parts in 12 root steps and six children. Steps 1–7: alternating 2×16, 2×8 and 6×10 plate layers with 2×2 plates with holes and Technic tiles with holes at the strut stations. Step 8: two 10202 6×6 tiles as the aileron bays. Steps 9–11: thirty-two 1×3 tiles in rows as the planking and the `step53-11` children (a 63082 socket plate pair) for the aileron balls. Step 12: four `step53-13` children (a 32294 suspension arm on a 2×2 plate with holes) as the struts, plus the `string8` and `string9` rigging children from string-end studs.
interfaces: All studs up except the angled struts. The struts' lower pin holes meet the lower wing and the cabane; the socket plates take the aileron towballs; the string-end studs anchor the rigging.
lesson: The upper wing of the biplane: a sandwich of 2×16 plates and 6×10 plates as the spar, rows of dark-green 1×3 tiles with gaps as the planked fabric-and-rib surface, 6×6 tiles as the aileron bays, two socket plates per side that take the ailerons' towballs, and four 1×9 suspension arms pinned underneath as the interplane struts.
parent_context: `10226 - main.ldr` places it at (−170, −212, 0) with matrix −1 0 0 / 0 1 0 / 0 0 −1, a 180° turn about Y, above the fuselage; the lower wing, cabane struts and ailerons are separate sections.
reuse_notes: Rebuild the technique: tile rows with one-stud gaps read as ribbed fabric on any vintage wing, socket plates give snap-in control surfaces, and suspension arms make slim interplane struts. The rigging strings are LDCad segments; add them last with the flex workflow.
